steps.title: Module boss
steps.body: Each task asks for a small reusable tool, the kind you would put in a `utils.py`. **Run checks** exercises them with a hidden harness.

steps.title: Memoize
prompt: Write a decorator `memo` that caches results by the positional arguments (a dict keyed by the `args` tuple). Calls with arguments already seen return the cached value without calling the function again. Expose the cache as `wrapper.cache`.
The tests decorate a slow recursive Fibonacci and check it stays fast and calls the inner function only once per argument.
template: return n if n < 2 else fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
Dojo.eq("a repeat call does no work", 81, len(calls))
Dojo.check("cache is exposed", isinstance(getattr(fib, "cache", None), dict) and len(fib.cache) == 81, "wrapper.cache should hold 81 entries")
hints: Use the `args` tuple as the dict key: tuples are hashable.
Recursive calls go through the decorated name, so they hit the cache too.

steps.title: Pipeline
prompt: Write `pipeline(*steps)` that returns a function taking one value and passing it through each step in order.
clean = pipeline(str.strip, str.lower, lambda s: s.replace(" ", "-"))
template: clean = pipeline(str.strip, str.lower, lambda s: s.replace(" ", "-"))
Dojo.eq("no steps returns the value", 5, pipeline()(5))
Dojo.eq("order matters", 7, pipeline(lambda x: x * 2, lambda x: x + 1)(3))
hints: Return an inner function that loops over `steps`, replacing `value` each time.

steps.title: Retry
prompt: Write a decorator factory `retry(times, exceptions=(Exception,))`. The decorated function is called up to `times` times; if it raises one of `exceptions`, try again. If every attempt fails, re-raise the last exception. Exceptions not in `exceptions` propagate immediately.
(You will meet `try`/`except` properly in module 6; the shape you need is:)
template: Dojo.eq("succeeds on the third try", "ok", flaky())
Dojo.throws("re-raises after all attempts", TimeoutError, broken)
hints: Loop `for _ in range(times):` with `try: return fn(...)` inside.
Remember the exception in `last`, and `raise last` after the loop.

steps.title: Windowed averages
prompt: Write a generator `moving_average(numbers, window)` that, for each position once at least `window` numbers have been seen, yields the average of the last `window` numbers, rounded to 2 places. It must work on any iterable and keep at most `window` numbers in memory (a `collections.deque(maxlen=window)` is perfect).
